minutes.headline: Planning Board opened hearings and sent a proposed multi-story self-storage project at 30 Summer Street to peer review.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board opened site plan and storm water hearings for a proposed multi-story self-storage facility at 30 Summer Street, questioned the applicant on parking, traffic, and flood-plain stormwater compliance, and voted to send the application to Graves for peer review before continuing the hearing to December 15th. The board also appointed Judy Dragos to the Economic Development Committee, reviewed and corrected prior decisions for signing, tabled a bond amount for a stormwater permit pending a cost estimate, and heard committee reports including ongoing Municipal Building Design Committee discussion of replacing the town hall annex.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to send the proposed multi-story self-storage project at 30 Summer Street out for peer engineering review.
The board then continued the 30 Summer Street public hearing to December 15.
Members questioned the applicant on parking counts, truck turning movements, and flood-plain stormwater compliance without resolving those questions.
A performance bond for a stormwater permit at 100/116 Towns Harbor Road was tabled until the applicant supplies a planting cost estimate.
Judy Dragos was appointed to the open seat on the Economic Development Committee.

why_it_matters: The 30 Summer Street self-storage hearing stays open through peer review, so its site plan, parking and stormwater design can still change before the board votes on approval.
The stormwater permit bond at Towns Harbor Road cannot be set, and won't be, until a cost estimate arrives -- delaying that permit.
Neither vote grants or denies a permit; both keep the applications in process for the December 15 meeting.
